RETAINING WALL + DECK (Will 9/27): the setbacks force a big, expensive retaining wall cut back into the hill here to make room. Put a deck on top of it: the view from up there is the best thing on the site, and a wall that costly should do something.
CULVERT / CONCRETE GUTTER (surveyed, FLOWLINE layer, el. about 1848-1850): stays. A big tube takes its water the last 30 ft or so down to the street. Erosion rivulets on the slope above it.

HILLSIDE ABOVE THE DECK AND GUTTER (Will 9/27): terrace, plant and irrigate. Main objectives: a fire-resistant landscape and water-wise management of the uphill grade; a new house must not get a landslide from above in a heavy-rain year. Trim up the pines.
STAIRS up the hill (east side, per A1.1 risers 7R@6, 3R@8, 9R@8, 5R@8): to be rebuilt.

WALL A on Will's lower line: the old pad wall goes, the yard is cut back to here at 1825; wall top 1832 (7 ft). Behind it the GARDEN TERRACE west of the steps: herb garden, rosemary over the wall, a concrete seat.

WALL B on Will's middle line, top 1840 (8 ft). Upper level: a concrete band along the wall from the steps to the round jacuzzi at the far west end (it looks over the low end of the roof); the rest planted.

THREE WALLS, each top ONE straight slope, higher west / lower east: C from the hill at its west end down to its east end; B rises above the flat pad as a sloping stem wall (4.5 ft -> 1.5 ft, a guard), opened at the top of the steps; A the same above the garden terrace (3.5 ft -> 0.5 ft).

STEPS (Will's plan markup): 11 risers with 21-in treads, 8 ft wide on the east edge, rising north from the yard onto the terrace's east end (the landing); then through a gap in wall B into a WELL between B and C, 13 risers rising west inside the band up onto the 1840 level.
DRAIN at the foot of wall C runs east to the existing downdrain; weeps behind A and B; each level slopes 2% to its wall. Pines kept just below the gutter, limbed up.
